core/r1_bounds.py::_perform_provider_cal.reason: The innermost provider call of the single dispatch path: the only place in the repository that calls a provider. Every guarded call and every producer dispatch ends up here, through benchmarks/r1_dispatch.py::DispatchGate.dispatch. The helper is private and it refuses a call that does not come from that dispatch method - the check is against the code object of the dispatch. The provider entry point is not captured: it is resolved from the provider object's own class at the moment of the call (core.r1_bounds._call_provider_entry_point), so the repository holds no provider callable at all - not in a closure, not in a registry and not in an attribute of a guard.

The invocation is REFUSED, not classified out of scope: benchmarks/run_iteration19_cpu_smoke.py::_assert_authorised raises SmokeNotAuthorised before the ephemeral app is started and before the provider's 'remote' is touched (the approval variable R1_APPROVE_ITERATION19_CPU_SMOKE is not set). A separate CPU-only app does not make an unauthorised remote workload authorised.

guard_implementation.core/r1_bounds.py: The guard itself: GuardedRemote (module-level functions), GuardedClass / GuardedClassInstance / GuardedClassMethod (the class methods, the bypass the review named) and GuardedProviderRemote (the guard installed on the provider object's own 'remote'). The guard holds no provider object: the raw objects live in the module-private registry of core.r1_bounds and the guard objects hold only an opaque token and the call-site name, so no attribute of a guard yields a raw provider callable. The guard holds no direct provider call - it delegates to the gate - so the repository has exactly one place that calls a provider: _perform_provider_call, the innermost step of the gate's dispatch, through _call_provider_entry_point. The provider entry point is not captured and not stored: it is resolved from the provider object's own class at the moment of the call, so no closure cell and no registry of the module holds an invocable provider callable. The class methods are guarded at their production boundary: the instance is moved to a subclass whose attribute resolution hands out the guard, so the method of the raw instance is guarded as well. The gate is not self-authorising: a provider dispatch additionally needs a verified approval (core/r1_approval.py), and R1 pins no approval key, so no provider dispatch is possible in R1.
